memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Joseph removed them from Israel's knees and bowed down with his face to the ground. And Joseph took both of them, Ephraim on his right toward Israel's left hand and Manasseh on his left toward Israel's right hand, and brought them close to him. But Israel reached out his right hand and put it on Ephraim's head, though he was the younger, and crossing his arms, he put his left hand on Manasseh's head, even though Manasseh was the firstborn." — Gen 48:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph arranges his sons carefully. Manasseh, the elder, is placed under his grandfather's right hand — the hand of the greater blessing. Everything is in its proper order.

And Jacob deliberately crosses his arms.

The text says he did it knowingly, "though he was the younger... even though Manasseh was the firstborn." This is not the confusion of a blind old man. It is a choice.

By now, this should not surprise us. Abel over Cain. Isaac over Ishmael. Jacob himself over Esau. God repeatedly bypasses the expected order and chooses the younger, the smaller, the one nobody would have picked.

He is not being random. He is showing us something about how His grace works. If God always chose the firstborn, blessing could be predicted by birth certificate. Instead He makes it clear that His favour rests on His own choosing, not on our natural qualifications.

Paul put it plainly: God chose the foolish things to shame the wise, and the weak things to shame the strong, so that no one may boast before Him (1 Cor 1:27-29).

If you have ever felt like the wrong candidate, you may be exactly the sort of person God delights to bless.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you assumed God's favour goes to the obviously qualified?
2. Where have you seen God bless someone nobody expected?
3. What would change if you stopped trying to qualify for grace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, Your grace does not follow the order I would expect, and I am glad. Thank You that Your favour rests on Your choosing and not on my qualifications. Amen.
